An opening request of $35 million leaves room to negotiate while prioritizing direct, automatic payments to class members. The separate fee does not affect our compensation; any reduction by the court should benefit the class.

The class can be paid automatically, so a claims process would unnecessarily reduce recovery. Open with a substantial class fund, a separately reviewable fee payable to the foundation, and no fee reversion. The demand leaves room to negotiate in light of certification risk and delay.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As interim class counsel, we submit that the proposed settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations with Brightline. The agreement provides a $31,250,000 class fund for approximately 400,000 identifiable members, with payments made automatically rather than through a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $2,000,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any amount not awarded will benefit the class rather than revert to Brightline. Class relief and fees were addressed during the same negotiation process; fees were not first discussed only after class relief was agreed. In our judgment, the substantial, direct recovery is fair in light of the risks of class certification, trial, and delay. We request preliminary approval, subject to the Court’s independent review and consideration of class members’ responses.
